transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Penumbra Partnerships), Liam O'Connor (Penumbra Cloud Architect), Dr. Raul Mendes (Penumbra ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Penumbra Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, im maya, im the ae for partnerships at redwood, with me is ethan, our solutions eng. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Asha Patel: good thanks, excited to learn more, we've been talking to a few infra partners and keen to see how a partnership could look.
[00:20] Ethan Park: awesome. high level for this call, we want to understand penumbra's platform, your partner objectives, technical requirements around latency/cost, and security/regulatory constraints. then we'll share high level partner program details.
[00:34] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. for context, penumbra is a managed cloud for data-intensive apps, we run multitenant clusters for SaaS customers and are exploring bundling LLM inference options for enterprise customers. main asks are: predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise security.
[00:50] Dr. Raul Mendes: yeah, also curious about model options — can you host both open models and commercial ones, and how easy is it to onboard our customers?
[00:58] Ethan Park: yes, redwood supports a catalog of open models and we also do integrations for customer-provided models. for partner mode we usually offer a few patterns: hosted api integration, dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), or private deployment inside customer VPCs or on-prem.
[01:15] Sofia Ruiz: from security side, we need SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, SAML/SSO support, detailed audit logs, KMS integration and options for customer-managed keys. also data residency for EU customers is a hard requirement.
[01:32] Maya Chen: totally understood. we have SOC 2, ISO-27001 summaries, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. for partner onboarding we can share a security pack, and partner private deployments can sit inside customer VPCs or on-prem for regulated workloads.
[01:48] Liam O'Connor: great. pricing caps and latency SLOs — how do you typically structure committed capacity?
[01:55] Ethan Park: dedicated uses reserved GPU pools with commit tiers; we provide throughput SLAs and can configure autoscaling and burst capacity. cost/per-token varies by model and quantization; we also have recommendations on batching and KV caching to optimize unit cost.
[02:12] Asha Patel: for go-to-market, penumbra wants an attachable partner offering: white-label, joint sales leads, revenue share. is that in your partner program?
[02:23] Maya Chen: yes, we have a partner tiering system — integrations partners get co-marketing credits, referral fees, and partner pricing on reserved capacity. for strategic OEM/white-label deals we do custom agreements. i'll send program overview after this call.
[02:38] Dr. Raul Mendes: technical question: if we run redwood runtime inside our clusters, what's the expected perf vs running on public cloud? and how easy is it to get reproducible benchmarks?
[02:50] Ethan Park: perf depends on hardware and model. our runtime has kernel selection, attention optimizations, and batching. when running on your infra we can run a benchmark harness — small set of prompts, target seq lengths — to give apples-to-apples numbers. usually we see close parity on comparable GPU families; of course network egress and instance types matter.
[03:08] Liam O'Connor: noted. we use a mix of A100 and some H100 testbeds in our lab. we also care about multi-tenant isolation and quota enforcement. can redwood integrate with our orchestration layer?
[03:18] Ethan Park: yes, we expose APIs and have an orchestration abstraction layer — you can pin model versions, set rollout policies, and use RBAC. for tenants we support isolation via dedicated pools or namespaced deployments in private mode.
[03:32] Asha Patel: competitor question — we've talked with paperspace and lambda labs; what differentiates redwood from those?
[03:38] Maya Chen: good question. redwood's differentiator is production-first tooling: built-in observability, trace-level latency/cost, and a unified runtime that supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with the same API. we focus on predictable unit economics and fallbacks for reliability.
[03:55] Sofia Ruiz: ok, security detail — do you support customer-managed keys (HSM) and can logs be shipped to our SIEM?
[04:02] Ethan Park: yes we support KMS integrations and can ingest logs to S3 or SIEM systems. for HSM it's something we do for private deployments; hosted requires a contract for customer-managed key options.
[04:15] Liam O'Connor: what's the onboarding timeline for a private deployment in our VPC?
[04:21] Maya Chen: typical onboarding is 4–8 weeks for a VPC/private control plane, includes infra prep, network connectivity, and security review. on-prem longer due to air-gapped requirements.
[04:32] Dr. Raul Mendes: for pilots, can we start with a hosted proof-of-concept to validate model quality, then move to dedicated?
[04:39] Ethan Park: absolutely. common flow is hosted POC -> dedicated reserved pools -> private deployment if needed. we have tooling to migrate model versions between modes.
[04:47] Asha Patel: on commercial terms, do you offer partner discounts on reserved capacity?
[04:51] Maya Chen: yes partner pricing and committed discounts are part of the program; for strategic partners we can do revenue share and co-sell arrangements. i'll include sample pricing tiers in the deck.
[05:00] [BREAK in transcript: short hold while screen share started]
[06:10] Ethan Park: ok jumping into a quick architecture sketch — redwood runtime runs on GPU nodes, has KV cache for prefix caching, batching layer, and a routing plane for fallbacks. for private mode there is a control plane that you can host or we can provide a private control plane in your VPC.
[06:35] Liam O'Connor: how do you handle model updates and rollouts? we need canary and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency spikes.
[06:44] Ethan Park: we provide canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies. the runtime can route to compatible variants to maintain SLOs.
[06:52] Dr. Raul Mendes: any constraints on model size for on-prem? we have some 70B and 200B model families to consider.
[07:00] Ethan Park: hardware is the main constraint; we support sharded execution and quantization-friendly paths. larger models may require multi-node configs; we can advise on quantization tradeoffs.
[07:12] Asha Patel: marketing/ops side — would redwood be open to joint webinars and a co-branded launch?
[07:18] Maya Chen: yes, co-marketing is usually part of partner package — webinars, case studies, and marketplace listing are standard.
[07:26] Sofia Ruiz: quick compliance note — our legal team will want a SOC 2 report and an endpoint security questionnaire. can you commit to PII data handling policies?
[07:35] Maya Chen: yes, we'll share the security pack and PII handling doc. for private deployments you can control data residency.
[07:44] [Timestamp jump — summarizing questions from penumbra] 
[07:50] Liam O'Connor: okay next up: integration specifics — do you have terraform modules or helm charts for private deployment?
[07:57] Ethan Park: we provide helm charts and terraform modules for infra provisioning. for large partners we also offer runbooks and automation scripts.
[08:06] Dr. Raul Mendes: good. on the benchmarking harness, can you run microbenchmarks on token latency and throughput and provide raw traces? we need numbers to compare to our existing inference stack.
[08:15] Ethan Park: yes, we can provide the harness and we'll run a set of DD tests: p99 latency, median latency, tokens/sec under steady-state load, and cold-start metrics. we'll also provide trace-level telemetry for deeper analysis.
[08:28] Asha Patel: timeline again — if we want a pilot in april, what would be the next steps?
[08:33] Maya Chen: next steps: i'll send the partner deck and pricing; ethan will set up a technical deep dive to scope the pilot; sofia will get security questions to us; we can sign an NDA if needed. goal is to kick the hosted POC by early april and then iterate.
[08:48] Sofia Ruiz: we will likely need an NDA before sharing certain customer lists.
[08:52] Maya Chen: noted, we can share a redlined NDA template.
[08:56] [09:00] Liam O'Connor: curious about SLAs — what uptime and latency SLAs do you commit to for dedicated?
[09:07] Ethan Park: dedicated has uptime SLAs and throughput targets; latency SLOs are model/tier-dependent. we can include specific numbers in the commercial proposal; typical committed latency windows for production tiers are p99 under X ms depending on seq len and model.
[09:23] Dr. Raul Mendes: ok. any common pitfalls partners run into?
[09:27] Ethan Park: common issues are under-provisioned batch sizing, not accounting for KV cache warm-up, and network egress configs. we help with profiling and recommend autoscale configs to avoid throttling.
[09:40] Asha Patel: let's talk a little about go-to-market motions; penumbra wants to resell under our brand and have an easy onboarding flow. does redwood support an OEM license?
[09:50] Maya Chen: yes OEM/white-label is possible for strategic deals; that typically involves additional legal work and co-branding agreements. we'll connect legal teams if you want to pursue that.
[09:59] [10:10] Ethan Park: quick note on integration: we have SDKs and REST APIs for generation, embeddings, and reranking. function/tool-calling is supported via structured output, which some customers use for agent-like features.
[10:26] Liam O'Connor: embeddings — we have customers who use vector search heavily. what's the embedding throughput and storage considerations?
[10:32] Ethan Park: embeddings are billed per unit; throughput is parallelized. we recommend batching and async ingest for large corpora. we also have guidance on vector store integration.
[10:42] Asha Patel: great. i think we have the info we need for now. next step for us is internal alignment and then the tech dive.
[10:50] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll follow up with the deck and security pack. ethan will reach out about scheduling.
[11:00] [11:05] Quick recap from maya:
- Share partner deck + sample pricing
- Schedule technical deep dive (infra + ml eng)
- Share SOC 2/ISO summaries and SSO/KMS integrations
- Agree pilot scope (hosted POC -> dedicated reserved pool)

[11:20] Asha Patel: thanks all, excited to dig in.
[11:23] Liam O'Connor: thanks.
[11:25] Dr. Raul Mendes: one follow-up — can you include a short checklist for pilot data requirements (format, size, target latency)?
[11:30] Ethan Park: yes we'll include that in the technical brief.
[11:33] Maya Chen: ok we'll get those over this week. thanks everyone.
[11:36] [END 15:24 local]

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript with occasional name mis-assignments, some words transcribed phonetically (e.g., 'KV cache' as 'K-V cash' in one segment), and short gaps during screen share.

References shared during call: partner deck (link: https://redwood.example/s/penumbra-partner-deck ), security pack (link: https://redwood.example/s/security-pack ), benchmark harness repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness )

Call ended with clear next steps and action items as listed above.
